name: Los Angeles
basis: City's second-unit ordinance became null and void on 2017-01-01 (SB 1069/AB 2299); the City applied the state default standards: ministerial approval, no owner-occupancy requirement, parking waived within 1/2 mile of transit (most of the city). City's own ordinance came later. Permits 80 (2016) -> 2,342 (2017).
sources: LA City Planning ADU information sheet (rev. Jan 2017), planning.lacity.gov/ordinances/docs/ADU/InformationSheet.pdf; Sightline Institute 2019-04-05, sightline.org/2019/04/05/la-adu-story-how-a-state-law-sent-granny-flats-off-the-charts/

name: San Diego
basis: Council approved companion-unit amendments to comply with state law in 2017 and waived several ADU fees around 2018 (resolution R-311730, superseded 2022); owner-occupancy and parking terms of the 2017 rules not verified, so not coded near-benchmark. Permits rose most from 2020-2023 (local ADU bonus program). Sensitivity: adoption 2018.
sources: sandiego.gov/sites/default/files/pc-17-043.pdf; sandiego.gov/sites/default/files/R-314270.pdf (2022 resolution citing R-311730); Bisnow, 'One Step Toward Defusing San Diego's Housing Crisis'

name: San Jose
basis: Local ADU amendments effective 2018-07-27 widened districts but kept one parking space unless exempt; not near-benchmark, so default 2020.
sources: sanjoseca.gov ADU ordinance updates page; SPUR letter 2018-06-19

name: all other jurisdictions
basis: No local near-benchmark adoption before the 2020 package documented; default 2020.
